Lessons.Title: Expressing Transformations of Functions Algebraically
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Create equations to represent known translations and reflections of a graph. Identify a transformation needed to fit a function to data and represent the new function with an equation.
Translations and reflections may be combined: g(x)=-f(x-2)+3 first moves inputs right2, then reflects output and raises3; order matters for some transformations.

Source activity 7.1: Describing Translations: Let \(g(x)=\sqrt{x}\). Complete the table. Be prepared to explain your reasoning. Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 7.2: Translating Vertex Form: Let \(f\) be the function given by \(f(x) = x^2\). Write an equation for the function \(g\) whose graph is the graph of \(f\) translated 3 units left and up 5 units. What is the vertex of the graph of \(g\)? Explain how you know. Write an equation for a quadratic function \(h\) whose graph has a vertex at \((1.5, 2.6)\). Write an equation for a quadratic function \(k\) whose… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 7.3: An Even Better Fit: In an earlier lesson, we looked at the temperature \(T\), in degrees Fahrenheit, of a bottle of soda water left outside for \(h\) hours. Let’s model this data with a function. This time, we will start with the function \(f(h) = 33(0.6)^{h}\). This graph has a shape that fits the data well. Describe a translation of this graph that fits the data. Write an equation defining a… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Practice Problem 1: Here is a graph of \(f(x)=e^x\) and a graph of \(g\), which is a transformation of \(f\). Write an equation for the function \(g\). Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: Describe the transformation that takes the graph of function \(f\) to the graph of function \(g\). \(f(x)=e^x\) and \(g(x)=\text-e^x+2.7\) \(f(x)=x^5\) and \(g(x)=(\text-x+3.1)^5+1\) \(f(x)=|x|\) and \(g(x)=|x|-26\) \(f(x)=\sqrt x\) and \(g(x)=\text-\sqrt{x-0.004}\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: Write an equation whose graph is a parabola with vertex at \((1,4)\) and which opens upward. Write an equation whose graph is a parabola with vertex at \((2,\text-3)\) and which opens downward. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 4: Describe how to move the graph so that it better matches the data. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: Here is a graph of \(y = f(x)\) for \(\text-10 \le x \le 0\). Sketch \(f\) for \(0 \le x \le 10\) if: \(f\) is neither even nor odd Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: Here are graphs of functions \(f\) and \(g\). Which sequences of transformations take the graph of \(f\) to the graph of \(g\)? Select all that apply. reflection over the \(y\)-axis, then translation up by 2 reflection over the \(x\)-axis, then translation up by 2 translation up 2, then reflection over the \(y\)-axis… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
